text:
sofia: Noticing a weird class of evictions in ap-southeast1 this morning. Pods requesting gpu:1 get scheduled but then quickly evicted with "Insufficient allocatable devices". Nodes show GPU free in DC metrics.

patrick: Any pattern on instance types or NVSwitch vs NVLink?

sofia: Pattern: newer racks with mixed GPU families (gpu-a and gpu-b) after we scaled a replacement pool. device-plugin logs show different device ID layouts: some nodes enumerate /dev/nvidia0..3, others map logical GPUs to indices 0..1 then 4..5. Pod's device allocation picks an index that kubelet later rejects during runtime.

mina: That sounds like the device-plugin/device-manager race we've seen before. If the allocation happens on the scheduler side to a logical index that isn't exposed by the runtime at bind time, kubelet evicts.

devops: Reproducer:```
# on affected node
nvidia-smi topo --matrix
# shows non-contiguous indexing
/dev/nvidia0  in use
/dev/nvidia4  in use
```
Pods scheduled there get device plugin allocation like: `Allocated GPU indices: [1]` but container runtime maps to `nvidia4` at start -> mismatch.

patrick: Oof. That explains "fits" then later eviction. Scheduler thinks resource fits (it sees ResourceGPU=1) but doesn't understand physical index contiguity.

ops: Cost implications: this increases churn and causes cross-AZ scheduling as workloads bounce, we've seen ~12% higher egress and packet rewarm from hot restarts.

pod-bot: Alert: 120 evictions in ap-southeast1 in last 2h matching pattern "allocatable mismatch". See: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/evictions/device-alloc-mismatch?var-region=ap-southeast1

mina: Short-term mitigation: drain and taint nodes with mixed families: `kubectl taint nodes <node> gpu.layout=mixed:NoSchedule` and scale up a homogeneous canary pool. Also update the device-plugin daemonset to delay registration until udev indexing stabilized.

sofia: I cordoned the two worst nodes and added taint. Requesting ops to block autoscaler from rejoining more mixed nodes.

patrick: Medium-term: patch our scheduler extender to query the device-plugin's /allocation API and prefer nodes where requested GPU indices map cleanly. We could also add a node label `gpu.index-layout=contiguous|sparse` set by cloud-init.

devops: We should also add an admission check to reject pods that request fractional device topology assumptions (e.g., specific indices) unless they have nodeSelector toleration.

ops: I'll open a ticket to throttle replacement ASG joins and update cost monitors. Also flag customer impact.

mina: Plan of record: 1) cordon/taint mixed nodes (done) 2) rollback unsafely-joined ASG (ops) 3) device-plugin change: wait for /dev stable + advertise consistent allocatable count 4) scheduler-extender PR to prefer contiguous-index nodes 5) migration job to evict low-priority pods safely w/ PDB respect.

sofia: Could someone sketch the migration job? I want to avoid mass restarts during peak 9-11am.

patrick: I'll author a k8s Job that labels pods `evicting=true` and then a controller that deletes them gradually:```
kubectl -n ml-serving label pod -l role=worker evictable=true --overwrite
# controller deletes 5 pods every 2m respecting PDB
```
I'll add a dry-run flag.

pod-bot: Incident INC-2026-149 created for device-index-allocations (ap-southeast1).

sofia: Thanks. Assigning: @mina (device-plugin change + tests), @patrick (migration job + scheduler-extender sketch), @ops (ASG rollback + autoscaler pause). We'll sync in 30m in #eng-platform. :thumbsup:

scheduler-bot: Note: consider adding scoring plugin for `gpu.index-layout` to avoid cross-family packing.
